_comment: The content and mode settings that choose what a part shows (lib/part-look-modes.mjs), as rules over the parts a block's locators find in the draft. The framework database gives these settings no CSS property or part, so the look pairing cannot place them; each names the setting it writes and the draft evidence that decides it (a part the draft draws or does not draw, the part's own words, a computed value). A rule whose setting the database does not hold for the block is a gap row; a setting that is not listed here is never written by the route.

rules.gap: the block holds one button action for every card; where the draft's button does different things per product, the catalogue writes each product's own action (_sgs_card_cta_action, add or page) and the card reads it with cardContentSource product (includes/product-card-per-product.php), so this setting is only the action of a product with none

the block holds one primary-button style (primary, secondary or outline) for every card, and the per-product reader holds a product's button words and action, not its style; the draft styles its button per product

rules.note: the per-product badge, price note and button words the catalogue writes (_sgs_card_*) render only in this mode
the stars and count are the product's own reviews (includes/product-card-live-fill.php); a product with none shows no rating row while noReviewsText is empty, which the route never writes (D-5)
the colour dots: the card draws them from the product's own colour terms (includes/product-card-swatches.php)
the heart on the photo, saved in the visitor's browser
the brand wordmark over the photo; it needs the product's brand (brandName) to print
the saving badge over the photo; its words are the product's own (savingLabel)
the small tag beside the title; it prints only for a product holding the chosen attribute term or tag (attributeTagTaxonomy, attributeTagTerm), which the route does not choose
a description the draft shows at some widths only (hidden on a phone); the tier is written where the width differs from the tier above

woocommerce/product-filter-chips._comment: The shop's filter chips (F-6): a count drawn inside a chip is the chips block's count pill; the first chip pressed on load whose count is larger than every other chip's is the All chip (its words without the count are sgsChipAllLabel, its count pill sgsChipAllCount); a press of an unpressed chip that releases the pressed one is one at a time (sgsChipSingle), one that keeps it is several at a time. A row with no counts proves no All chip, so its label is left unwritten. A chip colour the look pairing writes (WooCommerce's own customChip* settings) turns sgsChipPaintButtons on, which prints them on the chip buttons.

rules.reason: WooCommerce's chip colours paint the chip buttons only with this switch on (includes/product-filter-look.php)

rules.note: price-row is the parent of the price the shop parts record locates by structure (its `price` rule); a draft that draws the price only inside its controls (a pack tile, the add button) has none, and a draft that draws a price row keeps the block's own. loose-price (a bare amount on the page outside every control and every repeated card) must be absent too: a price the record does not locate ("From £9.50", a price inside a condition) keeps the row
the catalogue writes each product's recommended price to _sgs_rrp (lib/site-build-catalogue-php.mjs)

sgs/account._comment: The signed-in account views (surface my-account-in) and the sign-in forms (surface my-account). Each switch turns on the block's own view the draft draws: its orders as a list of cards (not a table), each card's thumbnails, an order's own page, the details form's phone field and marketing tick, its two columns and its password card, the address cards. `menu` is read by lib/part-look-account-views.mjs::accountMenuModes: which WooCommerce view each of the draft's tabs opens, told by the part its own view locates (or a view listing another component's cards), the endpoints the block's menu serves (each no tab opens is hidden), and the dashboard's parts switched off when it is hidden. The words rules write the draft's own words for the order page and the orders list, with the order number put back as {order}; the order numbers' shared prefix is the block's number prefix (Bean's D-7). `hideUnofferedTabs` is a rule with no condition: it is written on for every account surface, because a clone never offers a feature its shop lacks.

rules.reason: a clone never offers a feature its shop lacks: the menu leaves out Downloads while no product sells a download (Payment methods already follows WooCommerce)

rules.note: the draft draws its addresses as cards, which is the block's address editor (one card per address, edited in place); off is WooCommerce's list and separate form
Bean's D-7: the draft's order numbers are the client's own

menu._comment: lib/part-look-account-views.mjs::accountMenuModes. endpoints: per WooCommerce endpoint, the part its view locates (`part`) or a view listing another component's cards (`list`), the wording key its tab label goes to, the setting its view's heading goes to, and its count or tick switch. served: the endpoints the block's menu can show (the sign-out link is never hidden).

sgs/cart._comment: The basket drawer (surface header): what the panel shows and says, from the parts the drawer group locates in the draft, its empty state read with the basket emptied (part-look.json `empty`). A switch the draft gives no evidence for either way stays at the block default. The view link's style, the actions' layout and Remove's place come from the parts' boxes and paint (a box or a bare word; side by side or one below the other; at the right of the quantity or beneath it), each written only where the parts are drawn and agree at every width. Not decided here: the success words of the free-delivery bar (drawn only once the threshold is met).

woocommerce/checkout._comment: WooCommerce's fields (F-25): the label sits above its field where every label the draft draws sits above its field; a draft whose fields carry placeholders and no label keeps WooCommerce's floating label.

woocommerce/cart._comment: WooCommerce's fields (F-25): the label sits above its field where every label the draft draws sits above its field; a draft whose fields carry placeholders and no label keeps WooCommerce's floating label.
